items.followUp: Draw and label a simple diagram of an ATP molecule, showing its three main components.

rubric.why: Identifies the nitrogenous base and sugar that make up ATP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both are named.

rubric.why: Identifies the number of phosphate groups in ATP.
rubric.description: States that ATP has three phosphate groups.

rubric.why: Describes how the components are joined in the molecule.
rubric.description: States that adenine is attached to ribose and ribose to the phosphate group or chain.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either correct linkage.

rubric.why: Identifies the energy-rich bonds between phosphate groups.
rubric.description: States that the bonds between phosphate groups are energy-rich.

modelAnswer: ATP is a nucleotide made of the nitrogenous base adenine, a ribose sugar, and three phosphate groups.
Adenine is attached to ribose, and ribose is attached to the chain of three phosphate groups.
The bonds between the phosphate groups are energy rich; energy is released when the terminal phosphate is removed.

items.followUp: Briefly explain how forestry can be a career for a person with a biology background.

rubric.why: Identifies farming as a career where biological knowledge is applied.
rubric.description: Links farming or agriculture with biology.

rubric.why: Gives a relevant biological application in farming.
rubric.description: Mentions crop production, livestock care, pest control, or another suitable farming activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one suitable example.

modelAnswer: Farming is a career in which biological knowledge is used to grow crops and raise livestock.
Farmers apply biology to improve crop production, control pests and diseases, and care for animals.

items.followUp: What is one way data can be presented during data analysis, and what can scientists infer from it?

rubric.why: Explains that analysis organises or presents collected information.
rubric.description: States that data are organised or presented, such as in tables or graphs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one suitable statement.

rubric.why: Explains how analysis helps interpret results.
rubric.description: States that data analysis helps identify patterns, draw conclusions, or assess a hypothesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one suitable outcome.

modelAnswer: Data analysis organises and presents collected data, for example in tables or graphs.
It helps scientists identify patterns, draw conclusions, and decide whether the results support or reject the hypothesis.
